name: sales-pre-call-brief
expected_output: Backlog choice, then the five-part interview in order with the recipe in Part 3, a method follow-up for the step after the student stops, today-versus-ideal follow-up, fixed and gate questions, the four Part 5 draft messages, Value & Measurement close, the labels preview, and a saved single requirements file.
expectations: The first message contains the opening said exactly as in the spec (section 2), beginning "Deconstruct turns this workflow into a clear, testable description of what it must do.", followed by the switch line "I'll explain the questions that need it, and 'not sure' is always a fine answer. If you've done this before, say 'skip the explanations'."

Each part opens with "Part N of 5" and its name (Part 1 What this is worth … Part 5 Rules, where you check or approve its work, the sources it uses, and how you'll judge it), and no part announces its own time
Every AI message asks at most one question (a draft message ending "What's wrong or missing?" counts as one)
The label "Ask:" never appears in any AI message
The words step-driven and goal-driven never appear in any AI message, and the AI never asks the student to choose a path type

`requirements.md` has these sections in this order: `# [Name] — Workflow Requirements`, `## Goal`, `## Value & Measurement`, `## Metadata`, `## Path`, `## Inputs`, `## Context Inventory`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Example Scenarios`, `## Rules & Constraints`, `## Human Gates`, `## Security, Privacy & Safety`; no YAML frontmatter; no `Definition Type` row; no `## Sequence` and no `## Optimization Notes`
`## Human Gates` opens with the line `Runs: with you` or `Runs: without you`
`## Security, Privacy & Safety` contains the line `Governing regime: …` before a `### Writes` heading; under `### Writes` there is either a `- W1 · …` line or the line `None`
Every line under `## Path` that is a step is written `- Step N — [Name] · produces …` with a `fixed (…)` or `flexible` mark, tags in the spec's order
`framework/[name]/deconstruct-in-progress.md` existed during the interview (after Part 2) and is deleted once `requirements.md` is written
The close says "Workflow Requirements saved to `framework/[name]/requirements.md`." with the counts, names Step 3 Design and "run the design skill", and mentions `/design`
The Workflow node has `status: under-development`, links `[Requirements](framework/[name]/requirements.md)` in `# Artifacts`, and has no `definition_type` written by this run
Phase 1 asks "Which workflow from your backlog do you want to map?" with today's Why and Not sure? lines, and the Why does not mention step-driven
Part 2's last question is "Is there a law or regulation that governs this work?"; after "no", no detail table and no regulation questions appear
Part 3 shows the recipe by name: "We'll shape this in three steps: say it, sharpen it, make it checkable."
The goal sentence played back has no "containing" blank, and a second playback after the send-back test begins "Here's your goal now:"
`## Acceptance Criteria` uses the form `1. **AC1 (must)** — …` with one or two (must) checks and a `Reference example:` line naming the real output's C# ID
"never name another client" is recorded as a Must never rule in `## Rules & Constraints`, not as an acceptance criterion

The AI asks "What comes after that?" after the student's method stops, then "Is that how you do it today, or is it different?", then asks "Today you also … Should that stay?" about the LinkedIn-notes workaround
The CRM-check step is recorded as `fixed (policy)`
Decision line D1 is recorded with `settled by: a rule on a value`

Part 5 is delivered as four draft messages: messages 1–3 end "What's wrong or missing?"; message 2 introduces context with "These are the sources it uses, what we call its **context**"; message 4 ends with the Hand-it-back text
The test inputs are saved as `framework/[name]/inputs/E<n>-<short-name>.md`, numbered from E1, with E1 the input behind the Golden Example
